title: 4.3 Small Group · Group 2

noticeAndWonder.context: The arcade leaderboard shows one player scored 150% of the weekly goal, while a rare bonus round only adds a 0.5% point boost. How can a score be more than the whole goal, and how tiny is a 0.5% boost?

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Power-Up Boost
revealWordProblem.text: In the arcade game, your base score is 80 points. A rare power-up boosts your score to 250% of your base. How many points do you have after the power-up? (Hint: 250% means 2.5 times the base.)
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 250% = 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5, so 2.5 × 80 = 200 points. Because 250% is greater than 100%, the new score (200) is more than the base score (80).

turnAndTalk.question: The leaderboard shows one player hit 150% of the goal and a bonus round gives a 0.5% boost. How can a percent be more than the whole, and how can one be a tiny sliver?
turnAndTalk.kernel: 150% is more than one whole, and 0.5% is a tiny piece smaller than 1%.

vocabulary.term: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%

vocabulary.definition: Percents can describe amounts greater than one whole or smaller than one hundredth of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Los porcentajes pueden describir cantidades mayores que un entero o menores que una centésima de un entero.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.
vocabulary.cloze: A number out of 100, written with a % sign, is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: A percent bigger than 100%, more than the whole thing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje mayor que 100%, más que todo el entero.
vocabulary.cloze: A percent that represents more than one whole, like 150%, is ___.

vocabulary.definition: A percent smaller than 1%, a very tiny part.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How can a percent be more than the whole, or smaller than a tiny piece?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. In this group we go deeper: trickier numbers, a second way to see it, and explaining why it works — not just getting the answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To change any percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the decimal point two places to the left) — and you can explain why it works, even when it gets tricky.

onLevel.stem: A player scored 0.4% of the bonus points. Which decimal represents this percent?
onLevel.explanation: 0.4% = 0.4 ÷ 100 = 0.004. Move the decimal point two places to the left.
choiceFeedback: 0.4 es el número que está delante del signo %, no el decimal equivalente. Todavía falta dividir entre 100.
Move the decimal point left 2 places in 0.4%.
Check your decimal conversion carefully.
hints: 0.4% is less than 1%, so the matching decimal must be smaller than 0.01.
Divide the percent by 100: the decimal point moves two places left, and zeros fill the gaps.
Start at 0.4 and hop the decimal left twice: 0.4 → 0.04 → one more hop gives the answer's form.
onLevel.stemEs: Un jugador obtuvo 0.4% de los puntos de bonificación. ¿Qué decimal representa este porcentaje?
onLevel.explanationEs: 0.4% = 0.4 ÷ 100 = 0.004. Mueve el punto decimal dos lugares a la izquierda.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A rare item has a 0.8% drop chance. Write 0.8% as a decimal.

workedExample.label: Attempt
workedExample.work: The student divides 0.8 by 10 instead of 100, moving the decimal only one place.

onLevel.correctWork: To change a percent to a decimal, always divide by 100 — move the decimal point TWO places to the left, not one. 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008. So 0.8% = 0.008, which is far less than 1% (0.01), matching the tiny drop chance in the problem.
hints: Dividing by 100 moves the decimal two places, not one — dividing by 10 is a different operation.
0.08 would actually mean 8%, which is much bigger than the tiny 0.8% drop chance described in the problem.
onLevel.explanation: In the Attempt step the student divided by 10 and moved the decimal only one place. Percent to decimal always means dividing by 100, so 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008 — a value below 0.01, which matches a drop chance smaller than 1%.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso del intento, el estudiante dividió entre 10 y movió el punto decimal solo un lugar. Pasar de porcentaje a decimal siempre significa dividir entre 100, así que 0.8 ÷ 100 = 0.008, un valor menor que 0.01, que coincide con una probabilidad de aparición menor que 1%.

onLevel.title: Find the Percent Error

workedExample.label: Move the decimal two places left

onLevel.correctWork: 0.6% means 0.6 out of 100. Move the decimal two places left: 0.6 → 0.006. The correct answer is 0.6% = 0.006.
hints: The student only moved the decimal one place instead of two.
0.6% is less than 1%, so the decimal must be less than 0.01. 0.06 is too large.
onLevel.explanation: The step that moves the decimal shifted 0.6 only one place, landing on 0.06 instead of 0.006. Since 0.6% means 0.6 out of 100, the decimal point moves two places left, and the result must be below 0.01 because 0.6% is less than 1%.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso que mueve el punto decimal movió 0.6 solo un lugar y llegó a 0.06 en vez de 0.006. Como 0.6% significa 0.6 de cada 100, el punto decimal se mueve dos lugares a la izquierda, y el resultado debe ser menor que 0.01 porque 0.6% es menor que 1%.

onLevel.prompt: A game character has 300% of its original health after picking up a power-up. If the original health was 80 points, how many health points does the character have now? A student says 240 points. Another says 380 points. Who is correct and why?
onLevel.sentenceFrame: The student who said ___ is correct because 300% means ___ times the original, so ___ × 80 = ___.
onLevel.hint: If the character has 300% health after the power-up, think: what does 300% mean compared to 100%?
hints: 300% is three whole 100%'s — the health got MORE than the original, not less.
Convert 300% to a decimal (divide by 100), then multiply that decimal by the original 80 points.
Write 300% as 300 ÷ 100 = 3.0. Multiply 3.0 × 80 and compare your result with each student's claim.
onLevel.explanation: The student who said 240 points is correct. 300% means three whole 100%'s, so it is 300 ÷ 100 = 3 times the original: 3 × 80 = 240 points. The answer 380 comes from adding 300 to 80, which treats the percent like a plain number instead of a multiplier.
onLevel.explanationEs: El estudiante que dijo 240 puntos tiene razón. 300% significa tres veces el 100% completo, así que es 300 ÷ 100 = 3 veces lo original: 3 × 80 = 240 puntos. La respuesta de 380 viene de sumar 300 a 80, lo que trata el porcentaje como un número común en lugar de un multiplicador.

Divide the percent by 100, which is the same as moving the decimal point two places to the left.
Start at 0.5 and move the decimal point two places left, writing a zero as a placeholder wherever you need one.
hintsEs: Un porcentaje menor que 1% es una parte muy pequeña del entero: menor que una centésima.
Divide el porcentaje entre 100, que es lo mismo que mover el punto decimal dos lugares a la izquierda.

extending.stem: Could this really happen? Your phone shows it is charged to 0.5% — about how much of a 4,000 mAh battery is that?
choices: About 20 mAh — a tiny sliver, almost empty
extending.explanation: 0.5% = 0.005, and 0.005 × 4,000 = 20 mAh. A percent less than 1% is a tiny part, so the phone is nearly dead.
choiceFeedback: Think about what 100% means for a battery.
A percent over 100% would be more than full.
200 mAh sería 5% de la batería, no 0.5%. Revisa cuántos lugares se mueve el punto decimal al convertir 0.5% a decimal.
extending.stemEs: ¿Esto podría pasar de verdad? Tu teléfono muestra que está cargado al 0.5%. ¿Aproximadamente cuánto es eso de una batería de 4,000 mAh?
extending.explanationEs: 0.5% = 0.005, y 0.005 × 4,000 = 20 mAh. Un porcentaje menor que 1% es una parte muy pequeña, así que el teléfono está casi descargado.
hints: 0.5% is less than 1%, so the amount left will be a tiny sliver of the battery.
Change 0.5% to a decimal first, then multiply that decimal by 4,000 mAh.
0.5% becomes 0.005 as a decimal. Multiply 0.005 × 4,000 and notice how small the result turns out.
hintsEs: 0.5% es menos de 1%, así que la cantidad que queda será una porción mínima de la batería.
Primero convierte 0.5% a decimal y luego multiplica ese decimal por 4,000 mAh.
0.5% se convierte en 0.005 como decimal. Multiplica 0.005 × 4,000 y fíjate en lo pequeño que resulta.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — The Vanishing Boost

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: A bonus round gives a 0.5% point boost. Write 0.5% as a decimal.

workedExample.label: Final answer
workedExample.work: 0.5% = 0.5, so the boost is 50% — half the points!

extending.correctWork: 0.5% does NOT equal 0.5. To change a percent to a decimal, divide by 100 (move the decimal two places left): 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005. So 0.5% = 0.005, a tiny boost far less than 1% — not a huge 50% boost.
hints: Changing a percent to a decimal means dividing by 100, not just erasing the % sign.
0.5% is less than 1%, so its decimal must be less than 0.01. The answer 0.5 is way too big.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — el impulso que desaparece
extending.explanation: The mistake is in the step that just drops the percent sign: erasing % does not convert anything. Percent to decimal means dividing by 100, so 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005 — a boost far smaller than 1%, not the half-the-points 50% the student claimed.
extending.explanationEs: El error está en el paso que solo quita el signo de porcentaje: borrar el % no convierte nada. Pasar de porcentaje a decimal significa dividir entre 100, así que 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005, un impulso mucho menor que 1%, no el 50% (la mitad de los puntos) que dijo el estudiante.

Check: is this percent smaller than 1%?

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1% is treating every percent-to-decimal conversion the same way regardless of size — for example, writing 150% as 0.15 (as if it were an ordinary under-100% percent) instead of 1.5, or writing 0.5% as 0.5 (forgetting to divide by 100 at all) instead of 0.005. Before finalizing an answer, check that the decimal for any percent over 100% is greater than 1, and the decimal for any percent under 1% is less than 0.01.

optionalActivity.name: Extreme Percent Sort
optionalActivity.intro: Challenge — prove it: The arcade's leaderboard is full of wild percents — sort the tiny boosts from the giant jackpots, then figure out what each one really means! Convince a skeptic your answer is right.

diagram.title: 300% Jackpot of 30 Tokens
diagram.caption: The top bar is your 30 tokens (100% = one whole); the jackpot bar stacks three 30-token wholes, so 300% = 90 tokens — more than what you put in.

connect.scenario: A different arcade machine pays a jackpot of 300% of your tokens if you win. You inserted 30 tokens. One friend says the jackpot is 90 tokens. Another friend says it's 33 tokens.
connect.promptQuestion: Who is correct, and how many tokens does the jackpot pay?
connect.prompt: The friend who said ___ tokens is correct because 300% of 30 = ___ × 30 = ___. The other friend treated 300% as if it were ___% instead.

check.stem: What is 300% written as a decimal?

check.explanation: 3 × 30 = 90 tokens. The jackpot is three times what you put in.

check.stem: The other friend said 33 tokens. What percent of 30 is 33?
check.explanation: 33 ÷ 30 = 1.1 = 110%. That friend added a small amount instead of tripling — a common slip when a percent is over 100.

connect.modelAnswer: 300% = 3, so 300% of 30 = 3 × 30 = 90 tokens. The friend who said 90 is correct. A percent greater than 100% means MORE than the whole, so the jackpot is three times your 30 tokens. The friend who said 33 was really finding 110% of 30.

As a fraction, 0.25% is one quarter of one percent.
hints: Careful: 0.25% is NOT the same as 0.25. The % sign means it still needs to be divided by 100.
Convert 0.25% to a decimal first (divide by 100), then test each statement against that decimal.
Start at 0.25 and slide the decimal two places left: 0.25 → 0.025 → one more hop. Now check which statement matches.
